jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Core Fraud Services
jobs.description:
WHY SOCURE?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.





As the Senior Product Manager for Core Fraud Services at Socure, you will lead the development and expansion of the foundational platform that powers fraud decisioning across our entire suite of products. You will shape and scale key shared services, APIs, and machine learning capabilities, transforming raw fraud signals into high-performance risk intelligence. Your work will fuel faster innovation and more accurate fraud detection, raising the bar across the organization.

 

This is a highly technical platform product management role. Instead of owning a single customer-facing application, you will build the reusable infrastructure and core capabilities that enable a portfolio of fraud solutions. You’ll partner closely with Engineering and Data Science to deliver scalable, robust solutions that have direct impact on product effectiveness and organizational success.

 

Your role will be to translate business needs, customer feedback, and technical requirements into scalable platform features that power multiple fraud offerings. Success requires balancing long-term platform investments with immediate product and customer needs, while driving operational excellence and continuous innovation across the Socure ecosystem.

 

What you'll do:

Product Delivery & Execution:

 - Own Model Factory as a product, ensuring operational excellence while designing and improving systems that enable seamless customer adoption of the latest fraud intelligence. Continuously enhance model performance and manage the end-to-end model lifecycle, defining how AI and human oversight work together to deliver scalable, high-quality outcomes.

 - Manage and scale cross-fraud services like name matching and address validation, guaranteeing global consistency, high availability, and low-latency performance.

 - Lead the technical enablement for Score add-ons such as Graph Intelligence and Signals, architecting these core components for maximum reuse across Socure’s platform.

 - Apply structured product frameworks (e.g., RICE, Kano, JTBD, Opportunity Solution Tree) to drive data-based prioritization and tradeoff decisions.

 - Develop clear product requirements, acceptance criteria, and success metrics to support precise engineering execution.

 - Partner with Engineering and Data Science to ensure timely delivery and high quality of graph and signal-based features.

Integration & Value Realization:

 - Identify and execute opportunities to natively integrate graph insights into existing fraud and risk products, increasing detection rates and reducing false positives.

 - Collaborate with dependent teams to ensure seamless data flows, strong operational performance, and measurable customer value from graph-based systems.

 - Define and monitor KPIs for signal precision, system latency, and contributions to model accuracy.

Customer-Centric Problem Solving:

 - Conduct ongoing customer discovery and feedback loops to validate hypotheses and inform product direction.

 - Work with Customer Success and Sales Engineering to understand workflows and optimize usability.

 - Distill technical insights into actionable product value propositions for internal and external stakeholders.

Collaboration & Cross-Functional Alignment:

 - Collaborate closely with Data Science, Engineering, and allied product teams to ensure consistent, platform-wide integration of graph and signal intelligence.

 - Work with Product Marketing, Product Operations, and Account teams to produce documentation, release notes, and enablement materials that showcase product value.

 - Support quarterly planning and transparent communication on tradeoffs, outcomes, and progress.

Required Qualifications:

 - 5+ years in Product Management — specifically for platform systems, infrastructure, or core services in high-scale B2B API or ML/AI environments.

 - Demonstrated track record delivering technical products end-to-end, shipping on time, and iterating based on impact.

 - Technical expertise developing AI/ML-powered products, data platforms, or decisioning systems. Ability to closely partner with engineering and data science teams.

 - Proven strategic thinking and ability to develop and execute multi-year product roadmaps aligned to market and business objectives.

 - Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, including alignment across remote teams and diverse stakeholders.

 - Demonstrated ability to drive innovation using client feedback, market insights, and industry trends.

 - Excellent verbal and written communication, with comfort engaging with executive leadership and external partners.

 - Willingness to travel 10-15%.

Preferred Qualifications:

 - Experience building products for fraud, identity verification, risk, cybersecurity, fintech, payments, or financial services.

 - Client-facing experience within financial services, fintech, or government sectors.

 - MBA or advanced degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field.

 - 2+ years building B2B self-service products designed for both end customers and internal product users.

 - Strong user-centric product practices, with the ability to work hand-in-hand with Designers and Engineers.

 - Outstanding influence and cross-functional collaboration skills, with an ability to create clarity and drive focus.

Note: We cannot provide Sponsorship at this time.

You must be located in one of our talent hubs: SF, NY or Seattle.

jobs.title: Principal Product Operations Manager
jobs.description:
WHY SOCURE?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.




PRINCIPAL PRODUCT OPERATIONS MANAGER




ABOUT THE ROLE

Product Operations exists to give product teams the systems, data, and processes they need to plan, prioritize, and deliver well — the same way Sales Ops supports Sales or DevOps supports Engineering. This role sits at the center of that discipline, owning four things: the tools and systems product teams plan and work in, the reporting and analytics that give everyone visibility into what's happening, the process that makes planning and delivery repeatable instead of reinvented pod by pod, and the ongoing work of keeping strategy and execution connected as priorities shift.



We run Product Operations as a hybrid centralized/embedded model: some Product Ops work sits centrally and serves every product team consistently, while other Product Ops work sits embedded inside individual product lines, close to their day-to-day priorities. This role sits in the centralized hub — you're the shared systems, process, and reporting engine that every embedded product manager and product ops partner relies on, rather than being dedicated to any single product line.



We're a small team, so this role is intentionally broad. At larger companies, "owns the tools," "owns the reporting," and "owns the process" are sometimes split into two or three separate roles. Here, one person does all of it, with the flexibility to shift emphasis as priorities and team size change over time.




WHAT YOU'LL DO




OWN THE PRODUCT SYSTEMS & TOOLS STACK

 - Administer and configure the core product management / roadmapping platform (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, or equivalent) — workspaces, fields, workflows, scorecards, and permissions.

 - Own the connection between the product management platform and the engineering work-tracking system (e.g., Jira) — field mapping, status sync, and keeping data consistent between the two.

 - Manage the broader product tech stack: evaluate new tools, prevent tool sprawl, and maintain integrations across roadmap, delivery, feedback, and CRM systems.

 - Build and maintain the intake and prioritization workflows product teams use to submit, score, and rank requests.

 - Document system configuration and standard operating procedures so system knowledge isn't concentrated in one person (including yourself).


SUPPORT REPORTING & ANALYTICS FOR THE PRODUCT ORG

 - Build and maintain the dashboards and reports that give leadership and embedded product teams a reliable view of roadmap status, delivery progress, and portfolio health.

 - Define and track core product operations metrics (e.g., cycle time, roadmap adherence, planning hygiene, tool adoption).

 - Centralize and facilitate Product Performance metrics definition, telemetry builds, and availability to central data and BI teams, and coordinate dashboard and reporting builds with the central Business Intelligence team to enable deeper insights and faster decision making for the Product Team.

 - Partner with Finance, Sales/RevOps, and Engineering to bring commercial and delivery data (e.g., CRM/ARR data) into product prioritization and reporting.

 - Support recurring reporting cadences — business reviews, quarterly/annual planning, board updates — with clean, trusted data.

 - Monitor data quality and drive hygiene standards across the systems that feed reporting.


DRIVE PROCESS, EFFICIENCY & TEAM ENABLEMENT

 - Design and document repeatable processes for planning, prioritization, intake, and roadmap reviews — so teams have a consistent way of working instead of reinventing it pod by pod.

 - Identify friction points and manual, duplicative work in the product development lifecycle, and fix them — through better process, automation, or tooling.

 - Build templates, playbooks, and checklists (e.g., for feature intake, roadmap reviews, launch readiness) that save product managers time and reduce administrative burden.

 - Act as the go-to resource for product managers and embedded product ops partners on how to use shared tools and processes effectively — training, office hours, documentation.

 - Facilitate cross-functional handoffs between Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM so work moves smoothly instead of stalling on a handoff.

 - Continuously look for opportunities to standardize process across pods while leaving room for the flexibility each team actually needs.


KEEP STRATEGY AND EXECUTION ALIGNED

 - Partner with product leadership to translate high-level strategy and company priorities into a concrete, trackable roadmap and planning cadence.

 - Run the rhythm of planning — quarterly/annual planning cycles, roadmap reviews, and business reviews — that keeps execution connected to strategy as priorities shift.

 - Monitor progress against strategic priorities and flag early when day-to-day execution is drifting from what leadership actually intended.

 - Support trade-off and prioritization conversations when competing asks conflict with stated strategic priorities, so decisions get made deliberately rather than by default.

 - Make sure work happening inside individual pods visibly ladders up to company-level strategic themes, not just local priorities.

 - Close the loop after major planning moments — make sure decisions made in a review actually get reflected in the systems everyone works from day to day.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 10+ years in Product Operations, Business/Sales Operations, or a Product Analyst/Management role, ideally supporting or working inside of a product or engineering organization.

 - Hands-on experience working in or familiarity with a product roadmapping/PPM tool (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, Jira Product Discovery) and a work-tracking tool (e.g., Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps).

 - Comfort building dashboards and reports (in the PPM tool itself, Tableau, Looker, or Google Sheets/Excel); SQL is a plus.

 - Use of LLM-based tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) to augment and optimize job and role-related workflows, dashboards, research, etc.

 - Experience designing and documenting repeatable processes — intake, prioritization, planning cadences — rather than just running an existing one.

 - Working knowledge of PDLC and SDLC processes — roadmaps, backlogs, sprints, and prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, WSJF), different types of launch and product profiles (0-1 products, mature products, etc) and the PDLC process to support them.

 - Comfort facilitating conversations where strategic priorities and day-to-day execution are in tension, and helping stakeholders land on a decision.

 - Strong analytical skills — able to turn messy or scattered data into something people can act on.

 - A generalist mindset and genuine comfort moving between technical configuration, process design, and data/reporting work in the same week.

 - A bias toward noticing inefficiency and fixing it, even when it falls outside the "official" scope of the role.

 - Excellent documentation and communication skills — you're the connective tissue between central leadership and embedded product teams.

 - Ability to work autonomously on a small, fast-moving team where priorities shift.




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Product teams move faster and make better decisions when the systems, process, and data behind their work are trustworthy. Without a dedicated owner, strategy and execution tend to drift apart — teams stay busy, but on priorities that no longer reflect what leadership actually needs. In a centralized/embedded Product Ops model, this role is the connective tissue: it's why a PM on any pod can trust the roadmap data, why a planning decision made in a leadership review actually shows up in what gets built next sprint, and why leadership can get a straight answer about where things stand. As the team grows, this role can naturally split into two or three — Systems & Tools, Process, and Data & Analytics — but today it's one person who can support all of it.

jobs.description:
WHY SOCURE?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.







ABOUT THE ROLE



Socure’s rapid growth requires investment in a sophisticated launch process - one that keeps up with increasing volume, while making sure that we are continually raising the bar and working from the same page across the organization.



You will build and lead a small Launch Operations team that maintains clear visibility across upcoming product launches, and keeps cross-functional teams aligned leveraging the Product Manager (PM) owned launch checklist. For a start you will be the senior IC in this role as you prove value (see what success looks like below) for the rest of the team to be staffed. For the start you will need to prioritize the most essential elements to track and report on. So PMs will continue to quarterback product strategy, narrative, and customer readiness, while you (and eventually your team) provide the operational backbone to keep major milestones on track on the launch checklist.



Launches rarely fall behind because people don't know what to do; they slip because no single person owns making sure deliverables happen on time and with a clear backup plan. Your team will step in as that standing owner - not doing the launch deliverables yourselves, but guaranteeing everything is clearly assigned, dated, visible, and moving forward.



Sitting within Product Strategy & Operations, you'll collaborate closely with Product Marketing, Legal, RevOps, Engineering and other teams to make execution seamless and help product launches become world class




WHAT YOU'LL DO


RUN THE WEEKLY LAUNCH ACCOUNTABILITY FORUM

 - Set up and run a weekly launch check-in using a leaderboard developed and driven with our Product Manager input tool

 - Serve as the driving force in the room—spotting risks early, testing resolution plans, and keeping work moving forward without taking on the task execution yourself.

 - Maintain a consistent accountability cadence across all launch sizes—from major PR and investor launches to smaller feature updates and multi-tier strategic initiatives.




OWN THE LAUNCH CHECKLIST AND OWNERSHIP MODEL TO DRIVE PRODUCT ORG ACCOUNTABILITIES

 - Shift the launch checklist away from PMs managing every detail to direct task ownership by functional leads (e.g., Legal handles legal approvals, PMM leads product naming, Revenue Operations manages SKU setups).

 - Work with teammates in Product Operations to refine the checklist over time, adding or removing items as needs evolve and distinguishing true systemic gaps from one-off issues.

 - Share clear updates and digests with partner groups (PMM, Legal, Engineering, Support, RevOps) so open items stay top of mind naturally.

 - Keep teams aligned on execution discipline: if an item isn't assigned, dated, and visible, it isn't ready for launch.


TURN SYSTEMS INTO LAUNCH VISIBILITY

 - Pull target launch dates directly from roadmap tools like Aha! or Jira instead of relying on manually updated spreadsheets.

 - Establish clear criteria for when a feature enters the launch checklist process (typically 6–12 weeks before launch) and guide the initial workflow.

 - Adapt alongside Product Operations systems and tools as we automate tracking views and mature our operational system.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Executive leadership can understand the accurate status for any upcoming launch without needing to ask around for manual updates.

 - Every item on the launch checklist is owned directly by someone in the functional team doing the work. Your team will own raising awareness and visibility early and upfront

 - At-risk items get a clear recovery plan right away, and blockers are resolved or escalated

 - Our launch cadence scales smoothly across major releases and new capabilities for a start; and a potential for the team to partner with other functions like Technical Project Management teams for complex multi-team initiatives.

 - Commercial and field teams have timely, dependable visibility into launch timelines and feature availability, ideally with a rolling 90 day window view out

 - Prove the value first as the leading senior IC, and eventually build and lead a team that focuses on tracking launch health across key strategic initiatives, working directly with owning teams, and keeping status updates accurate.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 15+ years of experience in Product Operations, Program Management, or cross-functional tech operations inside product or engineering teams.

 - Proven experience running effective accountability rhythms (recurring reviews, status dashboards, operating cadence) that build trust and drive results through influence

 - Demonstrated success managing or building a team of contractors and FTEs from the ground up.

 - Comfort working with product roadmap tools (Aha!, Productboard) and issue tracking software (e.g. Jira, Linear); familiarity with spreadsheets and basic analytics is a must.

 - Good understanding of product and software development lifecycles across different launch scales (new products vs. enhancements

 - Strong meeting facilitation skills - able to guide discussions, align key stakeholders, and secure clear commitments.

 - Clear written communication style that makes progress updates and key takeaways easy to digest for leadership and partner teams.

 - Ability to establish practical, hands-on processes today while identifying opportunities to automate and scale over time.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience managing cross-functional go-to-market workflows across Legal, Product Marketing, Sales, Support, and Engineering.

 - Background in B2B SaaS, fintech, or another fast-moving technology space.

 - Experience building a team or operational function from scratch.

 - Bonus: Familiarity with CRM systems or connecting commercial data with product planning tools.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Identity Products
jobs.description:
WHY SOCURE?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.




SENIOR PRODUCT MANAGER, IDENTITY PRODUCTS


ABOUT THE ROLE



We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to build and take to market a new category of products at Socure: proactive identity notifications. These are subscription products that continuously monitor identities on our customers' behalf and push an alert when something material about that identity changes.



This is a zero-to-one role with a near-term launch. You will own the first product in this line end to end: defining what good looks like, closing any performance gaps that stand between us and a product customers will pay for, shaping the event contract and subscription model, and running it from beta through GA. More event types will follow close behind, and the scope will continue to expand as the portfolio grows.



Data is the heart of this role. The quality of a proactive notification product is the quality of the data underneath it: how much of the real world it sees, how accurate it is, and how quickly it knows. You will own that. You will establish the performance metrics that define success, decide what we need to source and what a candidate source has to prove, and make the call on which sources have earned their place and which have not. A dedicated Data Partnerships team runs discovery, negotiation, licensing, and vendor management against the brief you set, alongside data science and engineering.



You will also own commercialization. Pricing and packaging, commercial terms, early-adopter recruitment, beta and GA phasing, enablement, and coordinating every function to a launch date all sit with you.



This is a highly technical and highly commercial role. It suits a PM who is equally comfortable arguing about precision and recall methodology with a data scientist in the morning and defending a pricing model to the executive team in the afternoon.




WHAT YOU'LL DO




PRODUCT DEFINITION AND LAUNCH

 - Own the roadmap, definition, and launch of proactive identity notification products, from first beta customer through general availability.

 - Define the customer-facing event contract: what the notification contains, its lifecycle semantics, and how customers consume and act on it.

 - Design a systematic customer feedback loop so every notification we send makes the next one better.

 - Begin the product definition for the next event types on the roadmap, where the customer problem is more open-ended and the framing work is still to be done.


DATA SOURCE STRATEGY

 - Own what we source and why: define the gaps in our coverage, specify what a candidate source must prove, and set the bar it has to clear. Data Partnerships runs discovery and commercial negotiation against that brief.

 - Run rigorous, hypothesis-driven evaluations that measure incremental lift rather than headline coverage claims, and make the buy, build, or walk-away call.

 - Specify the licensing, retention, and derivative-use terms the product needs, and treat them as first-class inputs to every sourcing decision rather than an afterthought. Legal, Data Protection, and Data Partnerships paper the deal.

 - Hold the portfolio to its KPIs: decide which sources have earned their cost, which need renegotiating, and which to retire.


PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT AND KPIS

 - Define and instrument the KPIs for this product line, including coverage, precision, and recency, and build the internal benchmarking capability to measure them independent of customer-reported feedback.

 - Go a step further than measurement: define the target for each KPI that constitutes winning in the market. This requires competitive benchmarking and direct customer research, and it is the most important judgment call in the role.

 - Quantify the incremental value a subscriber receives per period, and use it to inform pricing and positioning.

 - Use SQL and analytics tooling to interrogate the data yourself rather than waiting on someone else's analysis.


ARCHITECTURE AND PLATFORM PARTNERSHIP

 - Partner with platform engineering teams to define how identity signals are resolved, merged across sources, and published, and make the architectural tradeoff calls on where that processing belongs.

 - Shape a generalized, reusable notification mechanism so each new event type is faster to ship than the last.

 - Balance latency, cost, and refresh cadence against the customer value each incremental improvement buys.


COMMERCIALIZATION AND GO-TO-MARKET

 - Define pricing, packaging, and commercial terms for a subscription product, in partnership with Legal, Finance, and Revenue.

 - Identify, recruit, and work hand-in-hand with early-adopter and design-partner customers.

 - Establish and track beta and GA phases, and coordinate cross-functional readiness, including end-to-end testing, to a committed date.

 - Build the positioning, marketing plan, and sales enablement materials with Product Marketing, and be the internal subject matter expert the field relies on.


CUSTOMER AND COMPETITIVE RESEARCH

 - Build a firm, evidence-based read on how we perform against market leaders and where our real differentiation lies.

 - Understand the bar customers will actually accept, and be willing to say which customers and use cases we should not sell to yet.

 - Assess and design around the business risk of getting a high-stakes identity signal wrong.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Experience: 5+ years in product management, preferably in identity verification, fraud prevention, data products, or other data- and ML-driven products.

 - Data product instinct: Demonstrated experience evaluating, acquiring, and operationalizing acquired data, including designing tests that isolate incremental lift and making the call to walk away when a source doesn't deliver.

 - Technical expertise: Strong understanding of APIs, SQL, databases, event-driven architectures, and product architecture generally.

 - Analytical skills: Comfortable working with data directly, writing queries, and defining measurement methodology, including precision, recall, and coverage benchmarking, to inform product decisions.

 - Commercial judgment on data deals: Has been the product voice in data or technology vendor negotiations; knows what to ask a provider to prove, how licensing, retention, and derivative-use terms constrain what you can build, and when a deal is not worth doing.

 - Commercial ownership: Experience taking a product to market, covering pricing, packaging, beta programs, and launch, not just shipping features.

 - Product judgment: Ability to balance technical complexity, customer needs, regulatory constraints, and business impact, and to set a defensible bar for "good enough to launch" when no precedent exists.

 - Customer focus: Experience working directly with customers, especially in complex or high-stakes environments.

 - Communication: Strong ability to explain complex technical and data concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, up to and including the executive team.

 - Collaboration: Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Engineering, Data Science, Legal, and go-to-market teams.


PREFERRED

 - Familiarity with consumer data regulatory frameworks such as GLBA and FCRA, and how they shape product and commercial design.

 - Experience with entity resolution, identity graphs, or record-linkage systems.

 - Experience building a subscription or usage-based data product from zero to first revenue.

jobs.title: Staff Product Operations Manager
jobs.description:
WHY SOCURE?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.







ABOUT THE ROLE

Product Operations exists to give product teams the systems, data, and processes they need to plan, prioritize, and deliver well — the same way Sales Ops supports Sales or DevOps supports Engineering. This role sits at the center of that discipline, contributing to three core areas: the reporting and analytics that give everyone visibility into what's happening, the process that makes planning and delivery repeatable instead of reinvented pod by pod, and the ongoing work of keeping strategy and execution connected as priorities shift.



We run Product Operations as a hybrid centralized/embedded model: some Product Ops work sits centrally and serves every product team consistently, while other Product Ops work sits embedded inside individual product lines, close to their day-to-day priorities. This role sits in the centralized hub — you're the shared systems, process, and reporting engine that every embedded product manager and product ops partner relies on, rather than being dedicated to any single product line.



We're a small team, so this role is intentionally broad. At larger companies, "owns the tools," "owns the reporting," and "owns the process" are sometimes split into two or three separate roles. Here, one person does all of it, with the flexibility to shift emphasis as priorities and team size change over time.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


SUPPORT REPORTING & ANALYTICS FOR THE PRODUCT ORG

 - Build and maintain the dashboards and reports that give leadership and embedded product teams a reliable view of roadmap status, delivery progress, and portfolio health.

 - Define and track core product operations metrics (e.g., cycle time, roadmap adherence, planning hygiene, tool adoption).

 - Centralize and facilitate Product Performance metrics definition, telemetry builds, and availability to central data and BI teams, and coordinate dashboard and reporting builds with the central Business Intelligence team to enable deeper insights and faster decision making for the Product Team.

 - Partner with Finance, Sales/RevOps, and Engineering to bring commercial and delivery data (e.g., CRM/ARR data) into product prioritization and reporting.

 - Support recurring reporting cadences — business reviews, quarterly/annual planning, board updates — with clean, trusted data.

 - Monitor data quality and drive hygiene standards across the systems that feed reporting.


DRIVE PROCESS, EFFICIENCY & TEAM ENABLEMENT

 - Design and document repeatable processes for planning, prioritization, intake, and roadmap reviews — so teams have a consistent way of working instead of reinventing it pod by pod.

 - Identify friction points and manual, duplicative work in the product development lifecycle, and fix them — through better process, automation, or tooling.

 - Build templates, playbooks, and checklists (e.g., for feature intake, roadmap reviews, launch readiness) that save product managers time and reduce administrative burden.

 - Act as the go-to resource for product managers and embedded product ops partners on how to use shared tools and processes effectively — training, office hours, documentation.

 - Facilitate cross-functional handoffs between Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM so work moves smoothly instead of stalling on a handoff.

 - Continuously look for opportunities to standardize process across pods while leaving room for the flexibility each team actually needs.


KEEP STRATEGY AND EXECUTION ALIGNED

 - Partner with product leadership to translate high-level strategy and company priorities into a concrete, trackable roadmap and planning cadence.

 - Run the rhythm of planning — quarterly/annual planning cycles, roadmap reviews, and business reviews — that keeps execution connected to strategy as priorities shift.

 - Monitor progress against strategic priorities and flag early when day-to-day execution is drifting from what leadership actually intended.

 - Support trade-off and prioritization conversations when competing asks conflict with stated strategic priorities, so decisions get made deliberately rather than by default.

 - Make sure work happening inside individual pods visibly ladders up to company-level strategic themes, not just local priorities.

 - Close the loop after major planning moments — make sure decisions made in a review actually get reflected in the systems everyone works from day to day.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Product teams and Leadership trust the systems and data they're working from.

 - Leadership can get a reliable answer about roadmap and delivery status without a scramble.

 - Tooling stays consistent and well-governed instead of fragmenting pod by pod.

 - Planning cycles run on schedule, supported by clean data rather than last-minute reconciliation.

 - Teams spend less time on manual coordination and administrative busywork, and more time making strategic decisions.

 - Roadmap execution visibly ladders up to strategic priorities — and when it drifts, that gets caught and surfaced early, not discovered at quarter-end.

 - Cross-functional handoffs happen through defined, repeatable processes instead of ad hoc effort every time.

 - System and reporting knowledge is documented and shared, not held by one person.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 6+ years in Product Operations, Business/Sales Operations, or a Product Analyst/Management role, ideally supporting or working inside of a product or engineering organization.

 - Comfort building dashboards and reports (in the PPM tool itself, Tableau, Looker, or Google Sheets/Excel); SQL is a plus.

 - Use of LLM-based tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) to augment and optimize job and role-related workflows, dashboards, research, etc.

 - Experience designing and documenting repeatable processes — intake, prioritization, planning cadences — rather than just running an existing one.

 - Comfort facilitating conversations where strategic priorities and day-to-day execution are in tension, and helping stakeholders land on a decision.

 - Strong analytical skills — able to turn messy or scattered data into something people can act on.

 - A generalist mindset and genuine comfort moving between technical configuration, process design, and data/reporting work in the same week.

 - A bias toward noticing inefficiency and fixing it, even when it falls outside the "official" scope of the role.

 - Excellent documentation and communication skills — you're the connective tissue between central leadership and embedded product teams.

 - Ability to work autonomously on a small, fast-moving team where priorities shift.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience operating inside a centralized or hybrid Product Ops model, supporting multiple embedded product teams or pods.

 - Experience facilitating OKR or strategic-planning cadences and connecting them to roadmap execution.

 - Working knowledge of PDLC and SDLC processes — roadmaps, backlogs, sprints, and prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, WSJF), different types of launch and product profiles (0-1 products, mature products, etc) and the PDLC process to support them.

 - Experience with CRM (e.g., Salesforce) or CRM-to-PPM integrations feeding commercial data into prioritization.

 - Background in process improvement (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, or similar) is a plus, though not required.

 - Experience in SaaS, fintech, or another regulated technology environment.

 - API or scripting experience (REST APIs, Zapier, or similar) for lightweight integrations and automation.

 - Experience supporting company-wide planning cycles — annual/quarterly planning, OKRs, board-level reporting.




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Product teams move faster and make better decisions when the systems, process, and data behind their work are trustworthy. Without a dedicated owner, strategy and execution tend to drift apart — teams stay busy, but on priorities that no longer reflect what leadership actually needs. In a centralized/embedded Product Ops model, this role is the connective tissue: it's why a PM on any pod can trust the roadmap data, why a planning decision made in a leadership review actually shows up in what gets built next sprint, and why leadership can get a straight answer about where things stand. As the team is growing, this role will be focused less on Systems & Tools; and more on Process enforcement, and Data & Analytics
